title: Vector-Borne Disease Control
tips: Empty, scrub, turn over, or dispose of items that hold water weekly (tires, buckets, planters, birdbaths).
Use mosquito repellents containing DEET or Picaridin on exposed skin and clothing.
Wear long-sleeved light-colored clothing outdoors to minimize mosquito attraction.
Install fine wire mesh screens on all windows and keep external doors closed at dusk.
Sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets, especially for infants and during daytime naps (Aedes protection).

title: Safe Drinking & Dining Practices
tips: Boil drinking water vigorously for at least 1 minute or use a certified UV/RO purifier.
Always wash hands with soap and water for 20 seconds before preparing or consuming food.
Eat freshly cooked foods while still hot; avoid room-temperature leftovers left uncovered.
Avoid ice cubes made from tap water and avoid pre-cut fruit from street vendors.
Store cooked foods and raw meats completely separately in clean containers.

title: Optimal Daily Fluid Balance
tips: Aim for 2.5 to 3 liters (10–12 glasses) of water daily under moderate climate and activity.
Increase fluid intake by +500 mL to +1,000 mL during high fever (>100.4°F) or vigorous exercise.
Check urine color: it should be pale light straw; dark amber indicates immediate fluid deficit.
Include natural electrolyte sources: coconut water, light buttermilk, lemon water, and clear broths.
Carry a reusable water bottle to maintain consistent sips throughout the day.

title: Airway Health & Infection Control
tips: Cover your coughs and sneezes using the inside of your elbow or a disposable tissue.
Ensure cross-ventilation in rooms by keeping windows slightly open for air circulation.
Wear an N95/KN95 respirator mask in crowded hospitals, clinics, or heavily polluted areas.
Avoid active and passive tobacco smoke exposure to preserve lung cilia and immune defenses.
Perform gentle saline steam inhalation or warm saline gargles for mild throat tickles.

title: Heart & Blood Pressure Protection
tips: Limit sodium (salt) intake to less than 5 grams (1 teaspoon) total per day across all meals.
Engage in at least 30 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise (brisk walking, swimming) 5 days a week.
Check blood pressure at least once every 6 months if under 40, and monthly if over 40.
Replace trans-fats and deep-fried palm oils with healthy oils (olive, mustard, groundnut in moderation).
Incorporate potassium-rich vegetables (leafy greens, bananas) to counterbalance vascular tension.

title: Blood Sugar & Weight Harmony
tips: Adopt the plate method: half plate non-starchy vegetables, one quarter lean protein, one quarter whole grains.
Avoid sugar-sweetened beverages, commercial fruit juices, and refined flour snacks.
Take a 10-15 minute walk immediately after meals to reduce postprandial glucose spikes.
Maintain waist circumference below 90 cm for men and below 80 cm for women (South Asian standard).
Screen fasting blood glucose and HbA1c annually if you have a family history of diabetes.

title: Immunization Defenses
tips: Ensure children receive all National Immunization Schedule vaccines (BCG, Polio, DPT, MMR, HepB).
Take annual seasonal influenza vaccines, especially pregnant women and senior citizens.
Adults over 50 and chronic lung patients should take Pneumococcal and Shingles vaccinations.
Receive Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV) for children in endemic typhoid belts.
Always consult a physician regarding booster shots before traveling to disease-endemic zones.

title: Restorative Cellular Recovery
tips: Aim for 7 to 8 hours of uninterrupted nocturnal sleep to regulate cytokine and immune balance.
Avoid screen use (phones, tablets, TV) for at least 45 minutes before sleep to support melatonin release.
Keep the bedroom dark, quiet, and cool for optimal deep sleep cycles.
Practice diaphragmatic breathing or mindfulness meditation to lower cortisol levels.
Maintain a consistent sleep-wake schedule even on weekends.
